name: Lattice QCD as a computational-physics workload
summary: Lattice field theory turns the Euclidean path integral into a very high-dimensional integral attacked with the whole computational toolkit: Markov-chain Monte Carlo, Krylov and multigrid solvers for the Dirac operator, and now ML samplers and tensor networks. Lattice QCD has in turn driven dedicated supercomputer design (APE, QCDOC).
sources: Wilson (1974). "Confinement of quarks". *Phys. Rev. D* 10, 2445. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445)

name: Neural tools shared by physics and HEP
summary: The same neural tools (classifiers, generative surrogates, normalizing flows, graph networks, anomaly detectors) serve physics in general and HEP in particular. In HEP they tag jets, emulate calorimeter showers, run in triggers and power simulation-based inference, and HEP was an early adopter and a main source of benchmark datasets.
sources: Carleo et al. (2019). "Machine learning and the physical sciences". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 91, 045002. [arXiv:1903.10563](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.10563)

name: Hybrid Monte Carlo: molecular dynamics in fictitious time
summary: HMC samples lattice gauge fields with dynamical fermions by adding conjugate momenta, integrating Hamilton's equations with a reversible, volume-preserving leapfrog or Omelyan integrator, and removing the integration error with a Metropolis step. It was invented for lattice QCD and later adopted in Bayesian statistics (NUTS in Stan).

name: Event generators as Monte Carlo integrators
summary: Event generators do importance-sampled (VEGAS-type adaptive) phase-space integration of factorized cross sections, hit-or-miss unweighting into events, and parton showers sampled with the veto algorithm. The shower samples the Sudakov no-emission probability with the same survival-probability logic used to sample radioactive decay times.

name: Euclidean action as a Boltzmann weight
summary: After Wick rotation, e^{iS} becomes e^{-S_E}, so lattice QFT is a statistical-mechanics problem sampled by Markov-chain Monte Carlo (heat bath, HMC). It inherits that field's problems: autocorrelation, critical slowing down toward the continuum limit, and the sign problem when the weight is not positive.
sources: Metropolis et al. (1953). "Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines". *J. Chem. Phys.* 21, 1087. [doi:10.1063/1.1699114](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1699114)

name: Tensor networks for lattice gauge theories
summary: In the Hamiltonian formulation, MPS and DMRG simulate 1+1D lattice gauge theories such as the Schwinger model without importance sampling, so they avoid the sign problem at finite density, with a θ term and in real time. Gauss's law can be built into gauge-invariant tensors, and these results benchmark quantum simulators of gauge theories.
sources: Schollwöck (2011). "The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states". *Ann. Phys.* 326, 96. [arXiv:1008.3477](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.3477)

name: Particle physics as the archetype of big science
summary: The path from cosmic-ray and accelerator discoveries to the Standard Model is a central case study in the history of physics. The field also defined 'big science': Lawrence's cyclotron laboratory, CERN (1954) as a model of international collaboration, and LHC collaborations with thousands of authors.

name: Naturalness as an argument form
summary: The hierarchy problem rests on naturalness, a fine-tuning argument that philosophy of physics studies as a heuristic. Its past success (the charm-quark mass estimated from K⁰ mixing) and the LHC's null searches for natural new physics have made its epistemic status an open debate.

name: Dispersive hadronic vacuum polarization for muon g−2
summary: Analyticity and the optical theorem turn the measured e⁺e⁻→hadrons cross section into the leading hadronic contribution to the muon g−2 through a Kramers–Kronig-type integral. Tensions among the e⁺e⁻ data sets (CMD-3 versus earlier experiments) and with lattice QCD are why this term decides the Standard Model comparison.

name: Holomorphy and the Virasoro algebra in 2D CFT
summary: In two dimensions the conformal maps are exactly the holomorphic functions, so the stress tensor splits into T(z) and T̄(z̄). Radial quantization turns charges into contour integrals, Ward identities and operator-product expansions follow from the residue theorem, and the Virasoro generators are Laurent coefficients.

name: S-matrix analyticity, dispersion relations and cuts
summary: Causality makes scattering amplitudes analytic in the energy variables, so they obey dispersion relations, the relativistic version of Kramers–Kronig. The optical theorem and Cutkosky rules give the discontinuities across branch cuts, and the modern unitarity method rebuilds loop amplitudes from their cuts.
map: \mathcal M(s)=\frac1\pi\int_{s_0}^\infty ds'\frac{\mathrm{Im}\,\mathcal M(s')}{s'-s-i\epsilon},\ \mathrm{Im}\,\mathcal M(s,0)=2E_{\rm cm}p_{\rm cm}\sigma_{\rm tot}

name: The Feynman propagator is a Green's function
summary: The propagator is the Green's function of the Klein–Gordon (or Dirac) operator, with the iε prescription choosing time-ordered boundary conditions, so the Feynman-diagram expansion is a Born series in Green's functions. Differential equations in the kinematic variables are also a main tool for evaluating loop integrals.
sources: Feynman (1949). "Space-Time Approach to Quantum Electrodynamics". *Phys. Rev.* 76, 769. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.76.769](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.76.769)

name: Neutrino mixing as a unitary basis change
summary: Flavour and mass eigenstates are related by the unitary PMNS matrix, so oscillation is the time evolution of a superposition of energy eigenstates. The two-flavour formula is the two-level Rabi formula, and the MSW effect is adiabatic passage through an avoided crossing of the matter Hamiltonian's eigenvalues.
sources: Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)

name: CKM matrix from bi-unitary diagonalization of Yukawas
summary: Quark mass matrices are diagonalized by separate left and right unitary rotations (a singular-value decomposition), and the CKM matrix is the mismatch between the up- and down-type left rotations. Parameter counting leaves (n−1)(n−2)/2 CP phases, one for three generations, and the Jarlskog invariant measures it independently of basis.
sources: Kobayashi & Maskawa (1973). "CP-Violation in the Renormalizable Theory of Weak Interaction". *Prog. Theor. Phys.* 49, 652. [doi:10.1143/PTP.49.652](https://doi.org/10.1143/PTP.49.652)

name: Instanton number as a Chern class; index theorem
summary: Instantons are classified by the second Chern (Pontryagin) number of the gauge bundle, and the θ term integrates that characteristic class. The Atiyah–Singer index theorem ties it to the Dirac operator's zero modes, which is the topological content of the axial anomaly.

name: Gauge fields as connections, field strength as curvature
summary: A gauge potential is a connection on a principal bundle and the field strength is its curvature, the same structures as the spin connection and Riemann tensor of general relativity. Wilson loops are holonomies, and a Bianchi identity holds in both.
breaks: The gravitational connection is soldered to the tangent bundle and fixed by the metric; internal gauge connections live on an abstract bundle with no metric to determine them.
sources: Yang & Mills (1954). "Conservation of Isotopic Spin and Isotopic Gauge Invariance". *Phys. Rev.* 96, 191. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.96.191](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.96.191)

name: Collider physics as measurement at scale
summary: Collider experiments use the full measurement chain: calibration, unfolding of detector response, systematic uncertainties as nuisance parameters, and blind analyses. HEP also produced much of the statistics toolkit physicists now share (Feldman–Cousins intervals, CLs, asymptotic profile-likelihood formulae).
sources: Feldman & Cousins (1998). "Unified approach to the classical statistical analysis of small signals". *Phys. Rev. D* 57, 3873. [arXiv:physics/9711021](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/9711021)
Read (2002). "Presentation of search results: the CLs technique". *J. Phys. G* 28, 2693. [doi:10.1088/0954-3899/28/10/313](https://doi.org/10.1088/0954-3899/28/10/313)

name: Axion haloscopes at the quantum noise limit
summary: Haloscopes such as ADMX convert dark-matter axions into microwave photons in a magnetized cavity, and the ~10⁻²² W signal makes the scan rate scale as 1/T_sys². Josephson parametric amplifiers at the standard quantum limit, squeezed states (HAYSTAC) and qubit-based photon counting are the enabling detector physics.

name: Calibration chains and resolution in collider experiments
summary: Collider experiments apply instrumentation principles at scale: test-beam and in-situ calibration with Z→ee and J/ψ resonances, luminosity from van der Meer beam-separation scans, and electronics noise and pile-up as limits on energy resolution.

name: Shared signal chain: sensors, preamps and noise
summary: In a particle detector, ionization or light becomes charge, which charge-sensitive preamplifiers amplify and shape, with thermal and shot noise setting the equivalent noise charge. Photomultipliers, SiPMs and silicon sensors are common to both nodes, and triggers are real-time filters working under bandwidth limits.

name: Profile likelihood, CLs and the 5σ discovery rule
summary: LHC searches are hypothesis tests: profile-likelihood ratios with systematics as nuisance parameters, Wilks/Wald asymptotics giving Z = √q₀, CLs for exclusions, and look-elsewhere corrections, as used in the 2012 Higgs discovery.
sources: Cowan, Cranmer, Gross & Vitells (2011). "Asymptotic formulae for likelihood-based tests of new physics". *Eur. Phys. J. C* 71, 1554. [arXiv:1007.1727](https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.1727)

ATLAS Collaboration (2012). "Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson with the ATLAS detector at the LHC". *Phys. Lett. B* 716, 1. [arXiv:1207.7214](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.7214)

name: Simulation-based inference and the likelihood-ratio trick
summary: When a simulator yields samples but no tractable likelihood, a classifier trained to separate θ₀ samples from θ₁ samples estimates the likelihood ratio, which by Neyman–Pearson is the optimal test statistic. Neural likelihood-ratio and posterior estimation now replace binned histogram fits in some ATLAS measurements.

name: Judging anomalies: systematics and correlated errors
summary: Whether an anomaly is real depends on its uncertainty budget. The muon g−2 comparison turned on the hadronic-vacuum-polarization error (mutually inconsistent e⁺e⁻ data versus lattice QCD, whose 2025 consensus value agrees with experiment), and the CDF W-mass outlier is a case study in combining correlated systematics across experiments.

name: The Standard Model as representation theory
summary: The Standard Model is defined by its gauge group SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) and by assigning each field to an irreducible representation, while Wigner's unitary Poincaré irreps label particles by mass and spin. Charges, multiplets and allowed couplings follow from group theory.
sources: Wigner (1939). "On Unitary Representations of the Inhomogeneous Lorentz Group". *Ann. Math.* 40, 149. [doi:10.2307/1968551](https://doi.org/10.2307/1968551)
Glashow (1961). "Partial-symmetries of weak interactions". *Nucl. Phys.* 22, 579. [doi:10.1016/0029-5582(61)90469-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(61)90469-2)

name: Strong CP problem and the Peccei–Quinn axion
summary: The QCD θ term is P- and T-odd and would give the neutron an electric dipole moment; the bound |d_n| < 1.8×10⁻²⁶ e cm forces |θ̄| ≲ 10⁻¹⁰. The Peccei–Quinn solution makes θ̄ dynamical: the axion, a pseudo-Goldstone boson, relaxes it to zero.
sources: Peccei & Quinn (1977). "CP Conservation in the Presence of Pseudoparticles". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 38, 1440. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440)
Wilczek (1978). "Problem of Strong P and T Invariance in the Presence of Instantons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 40, 279. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.279](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.279)

name: CP violation and the CPT theorem
summary: CP violation in kaons and B mesons is the experimental side of discrete-symmetry theory, and by the CPT theorem it implies T violation, since observed directly in both systems. With three generations the CKM matrix carries exactly one physical CP phase.
sources: Kobayashi & Maskawa (1973). "CP-Violation in the Renormalizable Theory of Weak Interaction". *Prog. Theor. Phys.* 49, 652. [doi:10.1143/PTP.49.652](https://doi.org/10.1143/PTP.49.652)

name: Parity violation built into chiral SU(2)_L
summary: Lee and Yang's 1956 proposal and Wu's 1957 cobalt-60 experiment showed that the weak interaction violates parity maximally. Electroweak theory encodes this by putting only left-handed fermions in SU(2)_L doublets (V−A currents), so the gauge representations themselves break P and C, while CP survives up to the CKM phase.
sources: Lee & Yang (1956). "Question of Parity Conservation in Weak Interactions". *Phys. Rev.* 104, 254. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.104.254](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.104.254)
Wu et al. (1957). "Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay". *Phys. Rev.* 105, 1413. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.105.1413](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.105.1413)

name: SU(5) and SO(10) embeddings of the Standard Model
summary: Grand unification is a group-embedding problem: SU(5) ⊃ SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) fits one generation into 5̄ ⊕ 10, and SO(10) fits it into a single 16 that includes ν_R. The embedding quantizes hypercharge and fixes sin²θ_W = 3/8 at the unification scale.
sources: Georgi & Glashow (1974). "Unity of All Elementary-Particle Forces". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 32, 438. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.438](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.438)

name: Graded Lie algebras evade Coleman–Mandula
summary: Coleman–Mandula rules out any Lie-group symmetry of the S-matrix that mixes spacetime and internal symmetries non-trivially. Haag–Łopuszański–Sohnius showed that the only loophole is a graded algebra with fermionic generators, which is supersymmetry, whose anticommutator closes on the momentum.
sources: Martin (1997). "A Supersymmetry Primer". [arXiv:hep-ph/9709356](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9709356)

name: Flavour SU(3) multiplets and colour singlets
summary: The eightfold way sorts hadrons into flavour-SU(3) octets and decuplets, and the Gell-Mann–Okubo mass formula predicted the Ω⁻. The quark model reads hadrons as colour singlets in tensor products of 3 and 3̄, and the same products list the allowed tetraquark and pentaquark structures.

name: SU(3) colour Casimirs set QCD dynamics
summary: Quarks sit in the fundamental and gluons in the adjoint of SU(3), and the group invariants C_F = 4/3, C_A = 3 and T_F = 1/2 fix the β-function, the splitting functions and the colour factors. Gluon self-coupling through the non-abelian structure constants gives asymptotic freedom, and large-N_c expansions treat N as a parameter.
sources: Gross & Wilczek (1973). "Ultraviolet Behavior of Non-Abelian Gauge Theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 30, 1343. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343)
Politzer (1973). "Reliable Perturbative Results for Strong Interactions?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 30, 1346. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1346](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1346)

name: Anomalies: Noether currents broken by quantization
summary: A classically conserved Noether current can gain a nonzero divergence from the path-integral measure. The axial anomaly explains π⁰→γγ, and its coefficient is topological: exact at one loop (Adler–Bardeen) and protected from further corrections.

name: Gauging a Noether symmetry; Ward identities
summary: Making a global symmetry local forces in a gauge field that couples to the Noether current, and Noether's second theorem says local symmetries give identities rather than new charges. In quantum theory these become the Ward–Takahashi and Slavnov–Taylor identities, which protect charge universality and renormalizability.
map: \mathcal L\supset-eA_\mu j^\mu,\ \partial_\mu j^\mu=0\Rightarrow k_\mu\mathcal M^\mu(k)=0,\ Z_1=Z_2
sources: Noether (1918; English translation 1971). "Invariant variation problems". *Transport Theory Stat. Phys.* 1, 186. [doi:10.1080/00411457108231446](https://doi.org/10.1080/00411457108231446)
Yang & Mills (1954). "Conservation of Isotopic Spin and Isotopic Gauge Invariance". *Phys. Rev.* 96, 191. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.96.191](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.96.191)

name: Higgs boson as the amplitude mode of electroweak breaking
summary: A Mexican-hat potential gives the Higgs doublet a vacuum value v = 246 GeV that breaks SU(2)×U(1) to U(1)_em, and three would-be Goldstones become the longitudinal W and Z (Higgs–Anderson mechanism). The leftover custodial SU(2) gives ρ = 1 at tree level, and the Higgs boson is the radial (amplitude) mode.
sources: Englert & Brout (1964). "Broken Symmetry and the Mass of Gauge Vector Mesons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 321. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321)
Higgs (1964). "Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508)

name: Chiral symmetry breaking: pions as pseudo-Goldstones
summary: The quark condensate breaks SU(2)_L×SU(2)_R to SU(2)_V, so pions are pseudo-Goldstone bosons, light because quark masses break the symmetry explicitly. This is Nambu's superconductivity analogy carried into hadron physics, and chiral perturbation theory is its low-energy effective theory.
sources: Nambu (1960). "Quasi-Particles and Gauge Invariance in the Theory of Superconductivity". *Phys. Rev.* 117, 648. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.117.648](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.117.648)
Goldstone (1961). "Field theories with Superconductor solutions". *Nuovo Cimento* 19, 154. [doi:10.1007/BF02812722](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02812722)

name: Anomalous dimensions and dimensional transmutation
summary: Quantum loops break naive dimensional analysis: because a renormalization scale μ enters, correlators scale with the engineering dimension plus an anomalous dimension, a case of Barenblatt's incomplete similarity. Classically scale-free QCD likewise generates Λ_QCD, a few hundred MeV, from a dimensionless coupling.
sources: Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)

name: Electron g−2, the fine-structure constant and muon g−2
summary: With five-loop QED, the electron g−2 gives α to sub-ppb precision, but the two atom-recoil values of α (Cs 2018, Rb 2020) disagree by more than 5σ, which limits that test of QED. The muon g−2 then tests the whole Standard Model, hadronic loops included.
sources: Morel et al. (2020). "Determination of the fine-structure constant with an accuracy of 81 parts per trillion". *Nature* 588, 61. [doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2964-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2964-7)

name: The fine-structure constant runs
summary: CODATA's α⁻¹ = 137.035999177 is the Thomson-limit value of a running coupling: vacuum polarization raises α to about 1/128.9 at the Z mass, and the hadronic part of that running comes from a dispersion integral over e⁺e⁻ data. A 'constant' of this kind is a renormalized coupling quoted at a stated scale.

name: Natural units and mass-dimension power counting
summary: With ħ = c = 1, particle physics measures everything in powers of energy and converts back through ħc. The mass dimension of fields and couplings then decides renormalizability, and a coupling of negative dimension, such as G_F = 1.1663787×10⁻⁵ GeV⁻², signals a heavier scale.

name: Planck scale vs weak scale: the hierarchy
summary: Natural units turn the hierarchy problem into a ratio of scales, M_Pl = √(ħc/G) ≈ 1.22×10¹⁹ GeV against v = 246 GeV. Large extra dimensions (ADD) lower the fundamental gravity scale to the TeV range by diluting gravity over a volume, while a warped extra dimension (RS) produces the ratio as an exponential.
map: M_{\rm Pl}^2\sim M_*^{n+2}R^n,\ m_{\rm weak}\sim e^{-k\pi r_c}M_{\rm Pl}
sources: Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos & Dvali (1998). "The hierarchy problem and new dimensions at a millimeter". *Phys. Lett. B* 429, 263. [arXiv:hep-ph/9803315](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9803315)
Randall & Sundrum (1999). "Large Mass Hierarchy from a Small Extra Dimension". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 83, 3370. [arXiv:hep-ph/9905221](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9905221)

name: Eikonal phase as Hamilton's action; orbits from amplitudes
summary: At large impact parameter the scattering amplitude exponentiates into an eikonal phase equal to the classical action, and the deflection angle is its b-derivative, as in Hamilton–Jacobi theory. Modern amplitude methods use this to compute classical two-body dynamics (post-Minkowskian scattering), with the radial action mapping scattering angles onto bound-orbit precession.
map: \mathcal A\sim\int d^2b\,e^{-i\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf b/\hbar}e^{i\chi(b)},\quad \chi\simeq S_{\rm cl}/\hbar,\quad \theta\simeq-\frac{\hbar}{p}\frac{\partial\chi}{\partial b}

name: Liouville's theorem, emittance and beam cooling
summary: Beam optics is Hamiltonian, so phase-space density is conserved and the emittance (phase-space area) is an invariant that sets luminosity, and long-term tracking uses symplectic maps. Lowering emittance takes non-Hamiltonian tricks such as stochastic cooling, which was essential for the SppS W/Z discovery, or electron and ionization cooling.

name: Poisson brackets become commutators
summary: Dirac's rule replaces Poisson brackets by commutators divided by iħ, which turns Hamilton's equations into Heisenberg's. Canonical transformations become unitary ones, and the phase-space generators of symmetries become charge operators; for fields the equal-time bracket of φ and π becomes the canonical commutator.
map: \{A,B\}\to\frac{1}{i\hbar}[\hat A,\hat B],\quad \{\phi(\mathbf x),\pi(\mathbf y)\}=\delta^3(\mathbf x-\mathbf y)\to[\hat\phi,\hat\pi]=i\hbar\,\delta^3
breaks: The map is not a homomorphism on all observables. Operator-ordering ambiguities (Groenewold–van Hove theorem) mean it holds exactly only on a restricted algebra, such as polynomials of degree two or less.

name: Dirac constraints and gauge redundancy
summary: Dirac's theory of constrained Hamiltonian systems is the canonical structure of gauge theory. A_0 acts as a Lagrange multiplier, and Gauss's law is a first-class constraint that generates gauge transformations, so quantization needs either gauge fixing with Dirac brackets or BRST cohomology.
sources: Yang & Mills (1954). "Conservation of Isotopic Spin and Isotopic Gauge Invariance". *Phys. Rev.* 96, 191. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.96.191](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.96.191)

name: Hybrid Monte Carlo: fictitious Hamiltonian dynamics
summary: Lattice QCD with dynamical fermions samples gauge fields by adding fictitious conjugate momenta and integrating Hamilton's equations with a reversible, symplectic leapfrog integrator. Liouville's theorem and reversibility make the Metropolis accept/reject step exact; the method was invented for lattice QCD and later spread into statistics as HMC.
sources: Wilson (1974). "Confinement of quarks". *Phys. Rev. D* 10, 2445. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445)

name: Lagrangian field theory as the input to quantization
summary: QFT starts from the same Euler–Lagrange machinery with a Lagrangian density: generalized coordinates become field values at each point, their conjugate momenta are promoted to canonical commutators, and cyclic coordinates become conserved charges.
map: q_k(t)\to\phi(\mathbf x,t),\ L\to\int d^3x\,\mathcal L(\phi,\partial_\mu\phi),\ p_k\to\pi=\partial\mathcal L/\partial(\partial_t\phi)
sources: Hamilton (1834). "On a General Method in Dynamics". *Phil. Trans. R. Soc.* 124, 247. [doi:10.1098/rstl.1834.0017](https://doi.org/10.1098/rstl.1834.0017)

name: Minimal coupling and classical color (Wong) dynamics
summary: Under a gauge transformation the velocity-dependent Lagrangian L=½mv²−qφ+qv·A changes only by a total time derivative, which is the classical root of minimal coupling. Making q a color vector that precesses in the field gives Wong's equations, the classical mechanics of a Yang–Mills charge used in transport models of the quark–gluon plasma.
sources: Yang & Mills (1954). "Conservation of Isotopic Spin and Isotopic Gauge Invariance". *Phys. Rev.* 96, 191. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.96.191](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.96.191)

name: Instantons as least-action paths in the inverted potential
summary: Tunneling amplitudes are dominated by stationary points of the Euclidean action, which are classical trajectories in imaginary time, i.e. Newtonian motion in the inverted potential −V. The double-well instanton, Coleman's bounce for false-vacuum decay, and the Yang–Mills instantons that make θ physical are all built this way.

name: Stationary phase of the path integral is least action
summary: The path integral weights every history by e^{iS/ħ}, and as ħ→0 stationary phase selects δS=0, which recovers Hamilton's principle. The phase of the semiclassical propagator is Hamilton's principal function (Van Vleck–Gutzwiller), so the classical action carries over unchanged into QFT.
sources: Hamilton (1834). "On a General Method in Dynamics". *Phil. Trans. R. Soc.* 124, 247. [doi:10.1098/rstl.1834.0017](https://doi.org/10.1098/rstl.1834.0017)

name: Quark–gluon plasma as a near-perfect viscous fluid
summary: Deconfined QCD matter in heavy-ion collisions flows as an almost ideal relativistic fluid, and viscous hydrodynamics (relativistic Navier–Stokes/Israel–Stewart) turns the initial spatial anisotropy into elliptic flow. Fits require η/s close to the holographic value 1/4π, and Λ polarization shows a vorticity of ~10²² s⁻¹, the most vortical fluid known.

name: QCD parton cascades and turbulent energy cascades
summary: A jet's parton shower is a self-similar branching cascade that carries energy from the hard scale to soft scales, like a Richardson cascade. For medium-induced gluon branching the analogy becomes quantitative: democratic branching sets up a scale-independent, Kolmogorov–Zakharov-like flux of energy to soft gluons (Blaizot, Iancu & Mehtar-Tani 2013).
breaks: A vacuum shower is a quantum branching process driven by soft and collinear logarithms and ends in hadronization. There is no steady forcing or viscous dissipation range, so a true turbulent stationary spectrum exists only for the in-medium cascade.
sources: Kolmogorov (1941; English translation 1991). "The local structure of turbulence in incompressible viscous fluid for very large Reynolds numbers". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 434, 9. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1991.0075](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1991.0075)

name: Conformal invariance in two-dimensional turbulence
summary: Polyakov (1993) proposed describing 2D turbulence with a non-unitary conformal field theory. Simulations later showed that zero-vorticity isolines in the inverse cascade are SLE₆ curves, the same conformally invariant class as critical percolation hulls (Bernard et al. 2006).
sources: Belavin, Polyakov & Zamolodchikov (1984). "Infinite conformal symmetry in two-dimensional quantum field theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 241, 333. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X)

Kolmogorov (1941; English translation 1991). "The local structure of turbulence in incompressible viscous fluid for very large Reynolds numbers". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 434, 9. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1991.0075](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1991.0075)

name: Renormalization group for turbulence and anomalous scaling
summary: Field-theory RG has been applied to randomly stirred Navier–Stokes flow (Forster–Nelson–Stephen, Yakhot–Orszag) to explain Kolmogorov's −5/3 law and to build RNG turbulence models. Intermittency gives anomalous structure-function exponents ζ_p≠p/3, the analogue of anomalous dimensions, but no controlled small parameter is known.
sources: Kolmogorov (1941; English translation 1991). "The local structure of turbulence in incompressible viscous fluid for very large Reynolds numbers". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 434, 9. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1991.0075](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1991.0075)
Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)

name: Rutherford cross-section: classical = Born = tree level
summary: For the Coulomb potential, the classical orbit calculation, the quantum Born approximation and the exact quantum result all give the same Rutherford cross-section. In QFT it is the non-relativistic limit of one-photon exchange, the prototype t-channel pole 1/q⁴, with Mott and recoil corrections for spin and kinematics.
breaks: The coincidence is special to 1/r: for other potentials the classical and Born cross-sections differ, and the exact Coulomb amplitude carries a divergent phase because the force is long-range.

name: From Rutherford's nucleus to deep inelastic partons
summary: Large-angle scattering that followed the point-charge Rutherford law revealed the nucleus in 1911. The same logic at SLAC in 1968, where structure functions scaled instead of falling like a form factor, revealed point-like partons, which QCD's asymptotic freedom later explained.
sources: Gross & Wilczek (1973). "Ultraviolet Behavior of Non-Abelian Gauge Theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 30, 1343. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343)
Politzer (1973). "Reliable Perturbative Results for Strong Interactions?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 30, 1346. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1346](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1346)

name: Elastic-recoil kinematics of dark-matter direct detection
summary: WIMP–nucleus scattering is a two-body elastic collision whose recoil energy peaks when the WIMP and target masses match, which drives the choice of heavy targets (Xe, Ar, Ge) versus light ones for sub-GeV searches. The Earth's orbital velocity adds to the Sun's motion through the halo and produces the predicted annual modulation.
sources: Bertone, Hooper & Silk (2005). "Particle dark matter: evidence, candidates and constraints". *Phys. Rep.* 405, 279. [arXiv:hep-ph/0404175](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0404175)

name: Missing energy: from Pauli's neutrino to KATRIN
summary: Energy and momentum conservation in beta decay led Pauli (1930) to postulate an invisible neutrino, and the same kinematics now measures its mass from the shape of the tritium spectrum near the endpoint (KATRIN). At colliders, missing transverse momentum is how neutrinos and invisible particles are seen.
sources: KATRIN Collaboration (2022). "Direct neutrino-mass measurement with sub-electronvolt sensitivity". *Nature Phys.* 18, 160. [arXiv:2105.08533](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.08533)
Cowan, Reines et al. (1956). "Detection of the Free Neutrino: a Confirmation". *Science* 124, 103. [doi:10.1126/science.124.3212.103](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.124.3212.103)

name: Orbit determination to track fitting (Kalman filter)
summary: Reconstructing a charged particle's helix in a solenoid from detector hits is an orbit-determination problem. Gauss's least-squares method, devised for Ceres, and the Kalman filter, built for spacecraft navigation, became the standard HEP track and vertex fits, with multiple scattering treated as process noise.

name: EFT for the post-Newtonian two-body problem
summary: Non-relativistic GR (Goldberger–Rothstein) treats an inspiralling binary with EFT power counting in v, so integrating out potential gravitons gives the Newtonian and Einstein–Infeld–Hoffmann Lagrangians as Feynman diagrams. Finite-size effects enter as Wilson coefficients (tidal Love numbers), which reorganizes celestial-mechanics perturbation theory with particle-physics tools.

name: Feigenbaum universality as an RG fixed point
summary: Feigenbaum's constants come from a fixed point of the period-doubling operator acting on maps, which is a Wilson-style renormalization group in function space. The fixed point has one relevant direction (δ) and a rescaling (α), which explains why every unimodal map with a quadratic maximum shares the same exponents.
sources: Feigenbaum (1978). "Quantitative universality for a class of nonlinear transformations". *J. Stat. Phys.* 19, 25. [doi:10.1007/BF01020332](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01020332)
Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)

name: Pitchfork bifurcation and the Higgs potential
summary: The pitchfork normal form is gradient flow in the same quartic potential that the Higgs field has when μ² changes sign, and a bead on a rotating hoop is the textbook mechanical model of spontaneous symmetry breaking. Small oscillations about a Mexican-hat minimum split into a massive radial (Higgs) mode and a flat Goldstone direction.
breaks: A finite mechanical system has no true symmetry breaking quantum mechanically, since tunneling restores the symmetry; that needs infinite volume. There is also no gauge field to absorb the Goldstone mode, and the electroweak transition in the SM is a thermal crossover, not a bifurcation in time.
sources: Higgs (1964). "Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508)
Englert & Brout (1964). "Broken Symmetry and the Mass of Gauge Vector Mesons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 321. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321)

name: Lyapunov exponents and the quantum chaos bound
summary: Out-of-time-order correlators extend the classical Lyapunov exponent to quantum field theory, because their early-time growth e^{λ_L t} reduces to the classical exponent in the semiclassical limit. In thermal QFT, λ_L is bounded by 2πk_BT/ħ (Maldacena–Shenker–Stanford), and large-c holographic CFTs saturate the bound.
breaks: Classical Lyapunov exponents are unbounded, and the OTOC exponent generally differs from the classical one. A clean exponential window exists only at large N or in the semiclassical regime, and the bound has no classical counterpart.

name: Chaos in classical Yang–Mills fields
summary: Spatially homogeneous SU(2) Yang–Mills fields reduce to the almost fully chaotic x²y² Hamiltonian (Matinyan–Savvidy), a Hénon–Heiles-type system. Classical lattice Yang–Mills has positive Lyapunov exponents that scale with g²T, which is used to explain fast entropy production and thermalization of the early glasma in heavy-ion collisions.
sources: Hénon & Heiles (1964). "The applicability of the third integral of motion: Some numerical experiments". *Astron. J.* 69, 73. [doi:10.1086/109234](https://doi.org/10.1086/109234)
Yang & Mills (1954). "Conservation of Isotopic Spin and Isotopic Gauge Invariance". *Phys. Rev.* 96, 191. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.96.191](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.96.191)

name: Dynamic aperture, resonance overlap and Arnold diffusion
summary: Sextupoles and magnet errors make betatron motion a near-integrable Hamiltonian system. KAM tori bound the stable motion, while Chirikov resonance overlap and slow diffusion set the dynamic aperture and beam lifetime; Laskar's frequency-map analysis, developed for Solar System stability, is now used to design rings.
sources: Hénon & Heiles (1964). "The applicability of the third integral of motion: Some numerical experiments". *Astron. J.* 69, 73. [doi:10.1086/109234](https://doi.org/10.1086/109234)

name: Topological solitons, winding numbers and instantons
summary: Kinks, vortices, monopoles, Skyrmions and Yang–Mills instantons are all finite-energy or finite-action field configurations labeled by homotopy winding numbers and bounded below by Bogomolny bounds. Once quantized, solitons become particles: Coleman showed the sine-Gordon soliton is the massive Thirring fermion, and Skyrmions model baryons.

name: Integrability: KdV, Virasoro and 2D field theory
summary: The second Hamiltonian structure of the KdV equation is the classical Virasoro algebra, and the KdV conserved charges become the quantum integrals of motion of 2D CFT. Lax pairs and inverse scattering carry over to integrable QFTs with factorized S-matrices and to the Bethe-ansatz spin chains that give anomalous dimensions in planar N=4 super-Yang–Mills.
sources: Belavin, Polyakov & Zamolodchikov (1984). "Infinite conformal symmetry in two-dimensional quantum field theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 241, 333. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(84)90052-X)

Gardner, Greene, Kruskal & Miura (1967). "Method for Solving the Korteweg-deVries Equation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 19, 1095. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.19.1095](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.19.1095)

name: Synchronized neutrino oscillations from self-interaction
summary: When neutrino–neutrino forward scattering dominates the spread of vacuum frequencies Δm²/2E, neutrinos of all energies lock into a common precession at one synchronized frequency, much like mean-field (Kuramoto-type) locking of oscillators with all-to-all coupling. This 'synchronized oscillation' regime matters in supernovae and the early universe.
breaks: The neutrino dynamics is conservative spin precession in a strong collective field, not dissipative phase attraction to a limit cycle, and the locked state can become unstable (bipolar and multi-angle modes).
sources: Strogatz (2000). "From Kuramoto to Crawford: exploring the onset of synchronization in populations of coupled oscillators". *Physica D* 143, 1. [doi:10.1016/S0167-2789(00)00094-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0167-2789(00)00094-4)

name: Neutrino flavor mixing as coupled pendulums
summary: Two coupled pendulums have normal modes rotated by a mixing angle and exchange energy at the beat frequency, which maps onto flavor states as rotated mass eigenstates with P=sin²2θ sin²(Δm²L/4E). Slowly tuning one pendulum through resonance gives adiabatic transfer at an avoided crossing, the MSW effect, with the matter potential playing the role of the detuning.
breaks: Pendulums exchange classical energy, while neutrinos have quantum probability amplitudes. Real symmetric spring couplings cannot produce the CP phase, which needs three flavors and complex mixing, and wave-packet decoherence has no simple mechanical counterpart.
sources: Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)

name: Free fields as infinitely many normal modes
summary: In the continuum limit a chain of masses and springs, with each mass also tied to the ground by a spring, becomes the Klein–Gordon field, and Fourier normal modes decouple it into independent oscillators. Quantizing each mode gives Fock space, so particles are the quanta of normal modes.

name: Neutral-kaon mixing as coupled damped oscillators
summary: K⁰ and K̄⁰ evolve under a non-Hermitian 2×2 Hamiltonian M−iΓ/2, which matches two coupled oscillators whose normal modes (K_S, K_L) have very different damping and beat at Δm. In this picture CP violation is a non-reciprocal coupling between the oscillators, so a mechanical model needs gyroscopic or rotating-frame couplings.
breaks: The interference of decay amplitudes into shared final states (ππ), quantum measurement of strangeness, and the CPT structure of M and Γ have no classical analogue.
sources: Christenson, Cronin, Fitch & Turlay (1964). "Evidence for the 2π Decay of the K₂⁰ Meson". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 138. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.138](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.138)

name: Misalignment: axion field as a Hubble-damped oscillator
summary: The homogeneous axion field is a damped oscillator with Hubble friction 3H: it stays frozen while overdamped (m_a≪3H) and starts oscillating once m_a~3H. After that its number density is an adiabatic invariant (E/ω) that dilutes as a⁻³ and fixes the cold-dark-matter relic abundance, and large initial angles add pendulum anharmonicity.
breaks: The friction comes from cosmic expansion, not dissipation, so energy redshifts instead of heating a bath, and m_a(T) switches on through QCD effects near the QCD transition.
sources: Peccei & Quinn (1977). "CP Conservation in the Presence of Pseudoparticles". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 38, 1440. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440)
Weinberg (1978). "A New Light Boson?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 40, 223. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.223](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.223)

name: Torsion pendulums test large extra dimensions
summary: ADD models with sub-millimeter extra dimensions predict a short-range departure from Newton's inverse-square law. High-Q torsion pendulums limited by thermal noise (Eöt-Wash type) have pushed the allowed Yukawa range down to tens of micrometers, which excludes two large extra dimensions at the millimeter scale.
sources: Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos & Dvali (1998). "The hierarchy problem and new dimensions at a millimeter". *Phys. Lett. B* 429, 263. [arXiv:hep-ph/9803315](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9803315)

name: Breit–Wigner lineshape = driven damped resonance
summary: A resonance's cross-section has the Lorentzian of a driven damped oscillator, with ω²→s, γω→MΓ, Q=M/Γ, and the ringdown time corresponding to the lifetime ħ/Γ. LEP fitted the Z lineshape this way to fix M_Z and Γ_Z, and its invisible width gave three light neutrino species.

name: Mach cone and Cherenkov cone
summary: A charged particle moving faster than light's phase velocity in a medium emits a wavefront cone with the same geometry as the Mach cone of a supersonic body. The cone angle measures β, the principle behind RICH particle identification, threshold counters and Super-K's rings.
breaks: Cherenkov light is linear coherent emission from medium polarization, with a dispersive n(ω) that makes the angle and threshold frequency-dependent and the emitted energy tiny (Frank–Tamm). Sonic booms are nonlinear shocks.

name: Lüscher term: zero-point vibrations of the QCD string
summary: The confining flux tube between static quarks vibrates transversely like a string fixed at both ends, and the zero-point energy of its normal modes (ω_n=nπ/r) gives the universal Lüscher correction −π(D−2)/(24r) to the linear potential. Lattice QCD confirms it.
sources: Wilson (1974). "Confinement of quarks". *Phys. Rev. D* 10, 2445. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445)

name: Hill's equation and alternating-gradient focusing
summary: Transverse betatron motion in a ring obeys Hill's equation, a parametric oscillator driven by the periodic focusing K(s), so beam stability is a Floquet/Mathieu stability problem. Alternating-gradient focusing stabilizes the beam the way fast driving stabilizes the Kapitza pendulum, tunes must avoid parametric resonances, and the Courant–Snyder invariant is the action of the motion.

name: Secular terms and renormalization (Lindstedt to RG)
summary: Naive perturbation theory for the Duffing oscillator produces secular terms that grow like εt, much as loop corrections produce logarithms of the cutoff. Poincaré–Lindstedt removes them by renormalizing the frequency, and the Chen–Goldenfeld–Oono renormalization-group method shows that the RG flow of amplitude and phase is the multiple-scales amplitude equation.
map: \ddot x+x+\epsilon x^3=0:\quad x\approx A\cos\omega t,\ \ \omega=1+\tfrac38\epsilon A^2+O(\epsilon^2)

name: Flavor pendulum: collective neutrino modes as a top
summary: In a dense neutrino–antineutrino gas the flavor polarization vectors obey precession equations that reduce exactly to a gyroscopic (spherical) pendulum, a heavy top whose spin is set by the neutrino–antineutrino asymmetry. Bipolar collective flavor conversion in the inverted mass ordering is the inverted pendulum falling over (Hannestad, Raffelt, Sigl & Wong 2006).
breaks: The mapping is exact only in the homogeneous, single-angle, two-flavor limit. Multi-angle effects and spatial inhomogeneity (fast flavor instabilities) go beyond the pendulum.

name: Muon g−2: spin precession of a relativistic gyroscope
summary: The muon spin in a storage ring precesses like a torqued gyroscope (dS/dt=μ×B), and the experiment measures the difference between the spin and cyclotron frequencies, which is proportional to a_μ. Thomas–BMT precession adds an electric-field term that vanishes at the 'magic' γ≈29.3, which is why the electrostatic focusing does not spoil the measurement.
breaks: Spin is intrinsic with g≈2, so the ratio of moment to angular momentum differs from a classical body. Thomas precession is a relativistic kinematic effect, and the spin direction is read out through parity-violating decay.
sources: Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

name: Regge trajectories from a rotating relativistic string
summary: Modeling a meson as a rigid rotating string of tension σ with its ends moving at c, the energy and angular momentum integrals give J=M²/(2πσ), a linear Regge trajectory. With σ≈0.18 GeV² the predicted slope α'≈0.88 GeV⁻² matches the observed ~0.9 GeV⁻².
breaks: This is a classical idealization with massless ends: quark masses, the quantum intercept α₀ and string breaking all modify it.

name: HBT intensity interferometry → Bose–Einstein femtoscopy
summary: Hanbury Brown and Twiss measured star sizes from intensity correlations. Goldhaber, Goldhaber, Lee and Pais (1960) found the same Bose–Einstein enhancement for like-sign pions, and LHC experiments now use it to measure femtometre source radii in pp, p–Pb and Pb–Pb collisions.

name: Beam optics: ray-transfer matrices for magnet lattices
summary: Transverse beam dynamics uses ABCD ray-transfer matrices: drifts are free propagation, quadrupoles are thin lenses, and a FODO cell of alternating converging and diverging lenses gives net focusing (strong focusing). Chromaticity is the beam-optics version of chromatic aberration and is corrected with sextupoles.
breaks: A quadrupole focuses in one transverse plane and defocuses in the other, so net focusing needs alternating gradients. Beams also have emittance (Liouville in 6D phase space), space charge and nonlinear resonances, which passive optics lacks.

name: Diffractive elastic pp scattering as Fraunhofer diffraction
summary: High-energy elastic pp scattering (TOTEM at 13 TeV) shows a forward peak and a diffraction dip, like the Airy pattern of an absorbing disc in the momentum transfer √(−t). The optical theorem ties the forward amplitude to σ_tot, and a black disc would have σ_el/σ_tot = 1/2.
breaks: The proton is grey (σ_el/σ_tot ≈ 0.26 at 13 TeV) and grows with energy (Froissart ln²s). Its amplitude has a real part and spin dependence, so a single disc cannot fit the dip depth.

name: Axion-induced vacuum birefringence and dichroism
summary: With the coupling g a E·B, only the photon polarization component parallel to an external B mixes with an axion-like particle. A magnetized vacuum therefore becomes dichroic (real conversion) and birefringent (virtual axions), which PVLAS-type polarimeters search for. An oscillating axion background rotates linear polarization; this is the proposed explanation for a ~2–3σ hint of CMB cosmic birefringence.
map: -\tfrac{g_{a\gamma\gamma}}{4}aF_{\mu\nu}\tilde F^{\mu\nu}=g_{a\gamma\gamma}\,a\,\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B\ \Rightarrow\ \text{only }\mathbf E_\gamma\parallel\mathbf B_{\rm ext}\text{ mixes}

name: Flavour oscillation as birefringence; MSW as adiabatic following
summary: Two neutrino flavours behave like two linear polarizations, and the mass eigenstates like the axes of a birefringent plate, so the conversion probability has the same form as light leaking through crossed polarizers. Solar MSW conversion is the analogue of light adiabatically following the axes of a slowly twisted birefringent medium (the Poincaré/Bloch-sphere picture).
breaks: There are three flavours with a CP-violating phase and an absolute mass ordering, while light has only two polarization states. The phase comes from mass differences, not refractive-index differences.

name: Maxwell theory as abelian Yang–Mills
summary: Covariant electrodynamics is the U(1) case of Yang–Mills theory: the same action, field strength and field equations. Yang–Mills adds a commutator term that makes gluons and W bosons self-interacting, while photons do not interact with each other.
breaks: The non-abelian commutator gives cubic and quartic self-couplings, asymptotic freedom and confinement, none of which classical electromagnetism has.

name: Haloscope: axions drive a resonant microwave cavity
summary: In a static field B₀, dark-matter axions act as an oscillating effective current g ȧ B₀. This current drives the TM₀₁₀ mode of a tuned cavity when ω = m_a c²/ħ, as in Sikivie's haloscope (ADMX, HAYSTAC). Sensitivity depends on standard cavity quantities: mode form factor, volume, Q and tuning range.

name: Waveguide cutoff modes = Kaluza–Klein mass tower
summary: Confining a massless field in compact transverse directions quantizes its transverse momentum. Each guided mode then follows a massive-particle dispersion relation along the free direction, with the cutoff frequency playing the role of the Kaluza–Klein mass.
breaks: Conducting walls impose Dirichlet/Neumann conditions instead of periodicity, so TE/TM spectra (and the missing TM zero mode) differ from a KK circle, and the waveguide geometry produces no gauge field.

name: RF cavities accelerate collider beams
summary: Beams gain energy from the longitudinal E field of the TM₀₁₀ mode of resonant cavities. The achievable gradient (~30–40 MV/m for superconducting niobium in the ILC, ~70–100 MV/m for normal-conducting X-band in CLIC) sets the length and cost of linear colliders.

name: Axion electrodynamics: modified Maxwell equations
summary: Adding g a E·B to the Maxwell Lagrangian gives effective charge and current densities proportional to ∇a and ȧ. These are the field equations behind haloscopes, helioscopes and stellar-cooling bounds. The same equations with constant θ = π describe the magnetoelectric response of topological insulators.

name: Kaluza–Klein: electromagnetism from a fifth dimension
summary: Five-dimensional general relativity on a small circle reduces to 4D gravity plus Maxwell theory plus a scalar. The off-diagonal metric components g_{μ5} play the role of A_μ, and U(1) gauge transformations are reparametrizations of the circle. This is the ancestor of modern large and warped extra-dimension models.

name: Magnetic monopoles: Dirac quantization and GUT monopoles
summary: A magnetic charge makes Maxwell's equations symmetric, and Dirac showed that a single monopole would force electric charge to be quantized. Breaking a simple GUT group down to U(1)_em necessarily creates 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles of mass ~M_X/α. Their predicted overabundance helped motivate inflation; MoEDAL and IceCube searches have found none.
map: \nabla\cdot\mathbf B=\rho_m,\quad qg=2\pi n\ (\hbar=c=1,\ \text{HL}),\quad M_{\rm mon}\sim M_X/\alpha_{\rm GUT}

name: Quantized Maxwell field: the first quantum field theory
summary: A normal-mode expansion turns the free Maxwell field into independent harmonic oscillators, and quantizing them (Dirac 1927) gives photons. Gauge redundancy forced the Coulomb-gauge, Gupta–Bleuler and later BRST treatments that became the template for quantizing every gauge field.
map: H=\sum_{\mathbf k,\lambda=\pm}\hbar\omega_k\left(a^\dagger_{\mathbf k\lambda}a_{\mathbf k\lambda}+\tfrac12\right),\quad [a_{\mathbf k\lambda},a^\dagger_{\mathbf k'\lambda'}]=\delta_{\mathbf k\mathbf k'}\delta_{\lambda\lambda'}

name: Gauge transformations and the covariant derivative
summary: The freedom A→A+∂χ of electromagnetic potentials, paired with a local phase change of charged matter fields, is the gauge principle. Yang and Mills extended it to non-abelian groups, where A becomes a matrix-valued connection and the potentials become the fundamental fields.

name: Aharonov–Bohm phase as the Wilson loop
summary: The Aharonov–Bohm phase around a solenoid is the holonomy of the U(1) connection. Wilson made these parallel transporters the basic lattice variables (link variables) and used the Wilson loop as the order parameter for confinement (area law).
map: U_{x,\mu}=e^{iagA_\mu(x)},\quad W(C)=\prod_{\ell\in C}U_\ell\to e^{\frac{iq}{\hbar}\oint_C\mathbf A\cdot d\mathbf l}=e^{iq\Phi_B/\hbar}

name: Thomas–BMT spin precession and the magic momentum
summary: The muon g−2 experiment measures how much faster the spin precesses (Thomas–BMT equation) than the momentum rotates, in a 1.45 T storage ring with field mapped by proton NMR. At γ = 29.3 (3.094 GeV/c) the motional-E term from electrostatic focusing cancels, so a_μ follows from ω_a and B alone. Fermilab's final result (2025) reached 127 ppb.
sources: Aoyama et al. (2020). "The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in the Standard Model". *Phys. Rep.* 887, 1. [arXiv:2006.04822](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.04822)

name: Weizsäcker–Williams photons in ultraperipheral collisions
summary: Lorentz contraction flattens an ultrarelativistic charge's field into a transverse pancake, equivalent to a flux of quasi-real photons with a spectrum ∝ Z²α/ω. With the Z⁴ enhancement, Pb–Pb ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC act as a photon–photon collider, where light-by-light scattering and γγ→ℓℓ are measured.

name: E·B invariant as the chiral-anomaly density
summary: The pseudoscalar Lorentz invariant FF̃ ∝ E·B is the U(1) Chern–Pontryagin density. As a total derivative it has no classical effect, but it sources the ABJ anomaly: π⁰→γγ, and chiral charge pumping when E and B are parallel (the chiral magnetic effect).
sources: Adler (1969). "Axial-Vector Vertex in Spinor Electrodynamics". *Phys. Rev.* 177, 2426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426)

name: The photon as the unbroken U(1)_em combination
summary: Maxwell theory is the massless U(1) that survives when the Higgs breaks SU(2)_L×U(1)_Y. The electron charge is fixed by g, g′ and the weak mixing angle, and the Z is the orthogonal, massive combination — classical electrodynamics is the low-energy remnant of electroweak theory.

name: Shockley–Ramo theorem: signals from weighting fields
summary: The current that a drifting charge induces on a readout electrode (silicon strips and pixels, wire chambers, TPC pads) follows from Green's reciprocity. One solves Laplace's equation with that electrode at unit potential and all others grounded, and the induced current is the charge's velocity dotted into this weighting field.
map: i(t)=q\,\mathbf v(t)\cdot\mathbf E_w(\mathbf x(t)),\quad \nabla^2\phi_w=0,\ \phi_w|_{\rm readout}=1,\ \phi_w|_{\rm others}=0
